result.reason: The passage describes finding one or two bodies and removing them with their surrounding earth, which is precisely what the prose under 'Intro & 1-2 Bodies' discusses.

The passage describes the 20-amah search protocol, the rule for continuing the search when a body is found at the edge of 20 amot, and the principle that a body found in context of a graveyard cannot be relocated — all of which match precisely the prose of the '20 Amah Search' section.

All three items form a continuous gemara discussion raising the 'whose opinion is this?' challenge about the four-to-eight amot range and the twenty amot search, answering via Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda's baraita, and then re-raising the problem from the latter clause — exactly what the 'Problem Stated' prose describes in detail.
The passage is the gemara's answer that the mishna follows Rabbanan and involves examining along the diagonal, which is precisely what the 'Rabbanan & Diagonal' section's prose discusses.

The prose under 'Tosafot Math' explicitly quotes and explains both the diagonal objection (items 1) and then says 'This is first answer to the problem,' implying the infant-graves answer (items 2-3) follows as the second answer — and indeed the 'Tosafot Math' prose discusses both the diagonal challenge and the infant-graves challenge together, whereas the 'Infant Graves' prose (index 1) discusses only the infant-graves material, making index 0 the better home for all three items taken together.

Both items introduce the vineyard parallel dispute (the contradiction between Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon across cases), which is precisely what the 'Vineyard Parallel' section's prose describes — the gemara noting the parallel dispute about vineyard spacing where Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis take opposite positions.

All three items form a continuous unit — the contradiction, then its resolution for Rabbi Shimon (emergency/twilight burial rationale), then its resolution for the Rabbanan (disgrace/firewood rationale) — which is precisely what the 'Emergency vs Intent' prose describes in detail.
The hadran marks the end of the previous chapter and transition to the new mishna about beis kor land sale, which is precisely what the 'Beis Kor Measure' section's prose describes.
